evidence.description: FIND-001 RESOLVED: the manually-curated CALL_GRAPH_FILES list was replaced with a structural whole-tree scan (`find "$SKILL" -type f \( -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.py' \) ! -path '*/tests/*'`) matched against an invocation-shape regex (import/from-import/importlib/spec_from_file_location/subprocess/os.system/Popen/source/dot-source/python-bash-direct-call), so gates/publish-gate.sh and any future file are automatically covered instead of requiring manual enumeration

independently read in full: calls only gates/v0.sh and gates/v05.sh, writes the state/PUBLISHED sentinel -- zero reference to note-publish-live.py, confirming the scan's real-world result on today's disk state is correct, not merely trusted

the scan's own non-vacuousness is proven by a canary: a deliberately-injected `python3 ".../note-publish-live.py" --draft-key test` line inside a temp file under lib/ is confirmed DETECTED by the same INVOKE_RE before cleanup -- this is a genuine control proving the check can actually fail, not a check that always trivially passes
test-prop22a-live-publish-wiring.sh reports PASS in the real green-phase run (not merely present in source, actually executed)

FIND-002 RESOLVED: new case (e) sets eyecatch PRESENT (a real-shaped assets.st-note.com URL) with a body containing zero tags, isolating gate-3b (img_count<1) from gate-3a (eyecatch) -- asserts the refusal names 'ZERO tags' specifically and explicitly does NOT contain 'eyecatch NOT set', proving gate-3a did not short-circuit

read directly: confirmed the img_count<1 branch's own stderr wording ('has ZERO tags in its body ... expected >=1 visual figure per REQ-21') matches exactly what the new test asserts, not a paraphrase

FIND-003 RESOLVED: 3 new dedicated hermetic sub-tests, each intercepting note_browser_common via sys.modules before sys.path is consulted, exercise row_found=False, paid_checked=False (row_found=True), and price_filled mismatch (999 filled vs 500 expected) IN ISOLATION -- each asserts its OWN specific refusal wording AND asserts the OTHER two branches' wording is absent, proving exactly one branch fired per case

read directly: the 3 refusal message strings (有料 radio row / 記事タイプ could not be confirmed / price confirmed as X, expected Y) match verbatim what test-prop22c asserts -- the test is checking the real branch logic, not a mocked substitute for it
test-prop22c-price-type-refusal-branches.sh reports PASS in the real green-phase run

FIND-004 RESOLVED, verified by reading the actual control flow (not taking the docstring's claim on faith): `ctx = None` then `try: ctx, pg = open_editor_ready(...)` -- the open_editor_ready call now sits INSIDE the try block (previously outside it). `except Exception as e` catches ANY exception anywhere in the browser-session lifecycle (open_editor_ready through the click sequence) and re-reports it through the SAME clean-refusal stderr shape as every other gate ('note-publish-live: REFUSED ... an unexpected browser-session error occurred: {e}'), never a bare re-raise. `finally: if ctx is not None: try: ctx.close() except Exception: pass` closes the context exactly once and cannot double-close, because if open_editor_ready itself raises before returning, the tuple assignment never completes and ctx remains None in main()'s scope (so main()'s finally correctly skips closing what it never held) -- verified this is not a double-close risk by tracing both possible paths

open_editor_ready()'s own internal try/except now wraps launch_context()'s downstream calls (add_cookies/new_page/goto/the readiness poll): on ANY exception it closes the context it itself created (best-effort) BEFORE re-raising -- verified this means a partially-launched context can never be orphaned regardless of which caller (note-publish-live.py or note-set-single-price.py) invokes it, closing the exact leak FIND-004 identified at its source, not just at one call site

3 injected-failure sub-cases, all independently re-verified by reading both the test's mock wiring and the real green-phase output: (1) open_editor_ready's own add_cookies failure -> __RAISED__=True (re-raises, does not swallow) + __MSG__ carries the ORIGINAL exception text (not replaced) + __CLOSE_CALLS__=1 (closed exactly once, no leak); (2) main()'s open_editor_ready call itself raising -> rc=1, a clean 'REFUSED ... unexpected browser-session error' message naming the real exception text, zero 'Traceback (most recent call last)' string anywhere in captured stdout+stderr; (3) select_paid_price raising mid-session after a real ctx handle was obtained -> rc=1, clean refusal, zero raw traceback, AND __CLOSE_CALLS__=1 confirming the finally block closed the ctx main() DID hold a handle to. All 3 real assertions match the real captured output verbatim, not fabricated expectations

checked for a NEW defect (success masked as failure or vice versa): the except-block's refusal message for an exception occurring AFTER a real click attempt explicitly states 'if this happened after a click attempt, verify the draft's live status independently via lib/note-verify-live.py before assuming either outcome' -- this is an honest acknowledgment of ambiguity (REQ-22's independent verifier exists precisely to resolve it), not a silent mask of either outcome; confirmed a stray re-invocation after such an ambiguous rc=1 is itself safe because a second run would simply re-confirm/re-click 更新する (update) on an already-published draft rather than double-submitting a new publish -- no new safety defect found

test-prop22b's REAL invocation independently reconfirmed post-fix: precheck eyecatch=true/img_count=3, tool actually clicked 更新する, postcheck status remained 'published' -- the try/except/finally wrapping did not regress the genuine success path

FIND-005 RESOLVED: a genuine LIVE (not structural-only) regression test now exists for note-set-single-price.py, the refactor's ORIGINAL caller -- targets the real TEST draft n39ef09f828f7 (never the flagship, with the same hard-exit-3 safety guard pattern as test-prop22b), asserts real post-refactor stdout markers (SINGLE_PRICE_TYPE: paid, SINGLE_PRICE_VALUE: 500, both screenshot paths non-empty on disk), and asserts the tool's own output never mentions 投稿する/更新する

read directly: confirmed the SINGLE_PRICE_TYPE/SINGLE_PRICE_VALUE/SINGLE_PRICE_PANEL_SCREENSHOT/SINGLE_PRICE_SCREENSHOT stdout markers the new test asserts are the SAME markers this script actually prints -- the test is not asserting against an invented output shape

the live regression test's REAL captured run: SINGLE_PRICE_TYPE: paid, SINGLE_PRICE_VALUE: 500, both screenshots written to disk against the real TEST draft n39ef09f828f7 -- genuinely exercised, not skipped (the venv-cloak python + real cookies were present on this host)

re-verified CRIT-204 across the FULL, current test suite (not just the two files changed this round): the literal string nfb2ace9f0ed8 appears ONLY in test-prop22b-live-publish-real-click.sh and test-prop21b-single-price-live-regression.sh, and in both files exclusively as the FLAGSHIP_DRAFT_KEY safety-guard constant plus a post-hoc negative assertion that it never appears in tool output -- it is never passed as a --draft-key/positional argument to note-publish-live.py or note-set-single-price.py in any test file

re-confirmed unchanged from round 1: never imports/execs/subprocess-calls note-publish-live.py, never reads NOTE_COOKIES_FILE, stdlib urllib only, PASS = (status==200) AND (key_in_body OR title_in_body)
